html:
Hurricane Hattie was a powerful hurricane that struck Belize City on 31 October 1961, flooding most of the town and killing hundreds of people in British Honduras.

Belize City sits barely above sea level on the coast, and the storm surge swept through its wooden houses. It was the second great hurricane to hit the town, after one in 1931. Thousands were left homeless, and some survivors were housed in camps that grew into new settlements.

The disaster convinced the colonial government that its capital had to move away from the sea. The result was Belmopan, built in the hills of the interior and made the capital in 1970. Storms like Hattie and later Mitch shaped planning all along the Caribbean coast of Belize.
sum: Hurricane Hattie was a powerful hurricane that struck Belize City on 31 October 1961, flooding most of the town and killing hundreds of people in British Honduras.
